label: Steel
notes: A session builds the whole engine (nothing shared between sessions), applies its limits, registers the host call function, then evaluates 1 + 1 and reads 2 back in Rust. Limits: Engine::new_sandboxed() (no I/O primitives, dylib loading blocked) with the crate's `sandbox` feature (bounded equality recursion); no instruction or memory limit exists: Engine::with_interrupted stores a flag that the 0.8.3 VM never reads.
Memory: resident growth across 252 live sessions (stopped by memory budget), measured first in a fresh process.

Tool call: the guest calls a registered Rust function on its own stack. Median of per-batch means, 1,000,000 calls in batches of 1,000 after 100,000 warm-ups; mean 1.5952 µs, slowest batch 2.3872 µs per call; 1.5948 µs of CPU per call.

Session = Engine::new_sandboxed(): deep-clones a per-thread bootstrap kernel image, builds a macro Kernel, then compiles and runs the prelude; plus register_fn(call). The kernel image itself is built once per thread and is excluded by the warm-up session and warm-up runs.
Host fn is register_fn("call", fn(SteelVal) -> Result<SteelVal, String>); call and reply are immutable im-rc hash maps keyed by symbols (preallocated on the host side).
Guest loop is a tail-recursive local function; call_function_by_name_with_args runs it.

A Steel session deep-clones its bootstrap kernel and compiles its prelude, so sessions are large and slow to create: the memory phase stops at its growth budget well before 1,000 sessions, and the start phase runs only as many creates as fit its time budget.
Compute: not measured in the Rust host.
